title: Every workflow file must declare a top-level concurrency key (enforced by conftest policy)
answers: conftest fails with 'Workflow must declare concurrency explicitly'
add a new workflow without a concurrency block
why does the policy check require concurrency in every workflow
workflow policy check fails on missing concurrency
body:
Invariant: every top-level workflow file (one that has `jobs`) must declare a top-level `concurrency` key.
Enforced by .github/policy.rego:deny_workflow_without_concurrency, which denies when `input.jobs` is present and `input.concurrency` is absent. The message names the standard group and the per-run opt-out.
What breaks if skipped: the conftest policy check fails for that workflow file.
Constraints: the check tests presence only. Any concurrency block passes, including a no-op per-run group, so it does not prove that grouping was chosen. Composite actions (files with `runs` and no `jobs`) are skipped by the `input.jobs` guard, so do not expect this rule to cover them.
applies: Top-level workflow files in .github/workflows/*.yml checked by conftest against .github/policy.rego.
says: Pull request policy check fails because the new workflow is missing concurrency settings.
Continuous integration pipeline fails policy verification when concurrency is not declared.
New pull request workflow checks fail with an error about undeclared concurrency.
Prevent overlapping pipeline runs by enforcing concurrency rules across all workflow files.
A newly added build pipeline fails the compliance check on workflow run settings.
